references.text: These verses in Isaiah speak of knowledge of God's plans that is unknown to humans, similar to the knowledge of the last day that not even the Son or the angels know.
This verse in Daniel emphasizes that times and epochs are set by God alone, which resonates with the idea that only the Father knows the day and hour of the end of the world.
This verse in Matthew repeats the words from Mark 13:32 and emphasizes that no one knows the day or hour of the end of the world, not even the Son, but only the Father.
Luke also highlights that the Son of Man will come at an unexpected time, supporting the idea that the timing of the end is unknown.
In Revelation, it is warned that Jesus will come like a thief, and the time is unknown, which aligns with the message in Mark 13:32 that no one knows the day or hour.
